correctness.rationale: For zero-augmentation integer vectors, fifth-root Fourier decomposition and integrality of beta = S1/(1-zeta) give |S1|^2|S2|^2 = 5|Norm beta|. This proves the exact product >=2/sqrt(5), with equality exactly for cyclotomic units. Nearest-integer decomposition proves the universal asymptotic lower bound and injectivity; powers of the golden unit give the matching upper sequence. Explicit case analysis proves the two-sided B^2 inverse-Lipschitz bounds for every B>=2. A standalone checker independently computes 624 integer norms and validates 20 unit powers; finite tests are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Five equispaced measurements are the first natural sample count after the noninjective 3- and 4-site real first-harmonic grids. Exact measurement injectivity coexists with sharp unbounded-energy instability, and the theorem quantifies it by the optimal distance constant 2/sqrt(5), golden-unit equality sequences and a provably sharp quadratic condition-exponent. These facts give a nontrivial, reproducible benchmark for modulo Fourier acquisition rather than a generic restatement of injectivity.
